title: Platform adoption, capacity, and budget sync
next_steps: Redwood to send revised Dedicated commitment pricing (tiered) by 2026-07-20
Customer to provide Q3 usage forecast by 2026-07-23
Schedule 60-min performance bench with Jon and Diego w/c 2026-07-27
action_items: Maya Patel|Provide month-by-month forecast for Q3 usage|2026-07-23
Avery Chen|Send Dedicated pricing spreadsheet and burst policy doc|2026-07-20
Diego Martinez|Run KV-cache microbench with Oleander's 2K token prompt set and share results|2026-07-29
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-07-16
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Oleander - Head of AI), Jon Ruiz (Oleander - Eng Mgr), Elena Gomez (Oleander - Finance)
Recording link: https://redwood.fireflies.example/ff-20260716-48213
summary: Quarterly health check focused on adoption cadence, capacity commitments, and budgeting. Customer reported steady growth in inference calls for product recommendations, spikes around promotions, and a cost concern for high-latency tail. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated capacity and short-term burst capacity. Agreed to share Dedicated pricing tiers, customer to share forecast, and run performance bench for 2K token prompts to validate latency/cost estimates.
topics: Agenda: 1) Current usage and chargeback trends 2) Tail latency and retry behavior 3) Dedicated capacity options and burst policies 4) Cost optimization (batching / quantization / cache) 5) Next steps and timeline
transcript:
[00:00:00] Avery Chen: Okay, welcome everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:00:05] Maya Patel: Hey yep Maya here.
[00:00:07] Jon Ruiz: Jon on the line.
[00:00:09] Elena Gomez: Elena, finance.
[00:00:12] Diego Martinez: Diego, Redwood SE.
[00:00:15] Avery Chen: Great. We planned 45 minutes — hope that works. We'll focus on usage, capacity, and the budget asks you raised in the email.
[00:00:28] Maya Patel: Yup — we had a spike during the mid-June promo and our costs week-over-week look higher than expected. We want to understand Dedicated vs Hosted economics and whether burst capacity helps.
[00:00:40] Jon Ruiz: Also some tail latency questions; a few requests are hitting 800–1,200 ms which is impacting UX.
[00:00:45] Diego Martinez: Right. From the runtime side, tail is usually caused by seq-len variance and KV cache misses, plus occasionally cold-starts on the worker pool. We can show you the KV cache hit-rate and some batching profiles.
[00:01:00] Maya Patel: That would be helpful. For context, our average token length is about 350 but promotions have 1.8–2.2k token flows.
[00:01:12] Avery Chen: Noted. Quick check — are you currently on the hosted plan for all traffic?
[00:01:18] Jon Ruiz: Mostly hosted, yes. We have a small internal Dedicated pool for internal analytics but not for production features.
[00:01:25] Elena Gomez: From finance, we're trying to forecast Q3 commit. The hosted model's variable costs are spiking in promo windows and that's hard to budget for.
[00:01:34] Avery Chen: Makes sense. We'll go through Dedicated tiers — predictable monthly commit with burst — and show the cost break-even point.
[00:01:42] Diego Martinez: I also want to flag model variants — switching to a quantized variant or 8-bit mode for some endpoints can drop token cost 20–40% with minimal accuracy hit on recommendation tasks.
[00:01:54] Maya Patel: We're sensitive to quality on recommendations — conversion lifts can move the needle. Any evals you have for quantized recommender models?
[00:02:02] Diego Martinez: We have internal evals; I can run a sample on your prompt set. That was one of the bench items we suggested.
[00:02:09] Jon Ruiz: Great.
[00:02:11] 
[00:02:30] Avery Chen: Let's look at numbers — Maya, you sent last week's usage summary; can you quickly summarize the percent of traffic in the high-token tail?
[00:02:36] Maya Patel: Sure. About 12% of calls are >1k tokens but they account for roughly 35% of token spend. The rest are 200–500 tokens.
[00:02:49] Diego Martinez: That aligns with typical skew — small percent of calls accounting for large fraction of cost. Two levers: prefix/KV caching and request routing to a cheaper quantized model for long prompts.
[00:03:02] Jon Ruiz: On caching, we tried Redwood's prefix cache but weren't seeing much benefit because our prompts vary a lot. Are there suggestions on how to normalize?
[00:03:11] Diego Martinez: If you can canonicalize prompt templates — strip irrelevant session metadata and only cache the static parts — hit rates can improve a lot. We can provide a snippet for canonicalization in your SDK.
[00:03:22] Maya Patel: That would be useful, thank you.
[00:03:30] 
[00:03:55] Avery Chen: On Dedicated — typical setup: commit to N GPUs/month, predictable price, we give you burst capacity at a smaller premium and auto-fallback to Hosted if Dedicated is saturated. Pricing depends on GPU type and utilization.
[00:04:09] Elena Gomez: Can you send us an example contract for a mid-tier commit? We need to compare to our internal GPU costs for a TCO analysis.
[00:04:16] Avery Chen: Yes. I'll attach the Dedicated pricing spreadsheet and the burst policy doc after the call.
[00:04:22] Diego Martinez: Also worth noting: with Dedicated you can pin model versions to avoid surprises during rollouts, which helps ops predict behavior during high traffic.
[00:04:32] Jon Ruiz: Pinning is appealing. We've had at least one incident where a model change increased latency unexpectedly.
[00:04:37] 
[00:04:58] Maya Patel: Another question on security and compliance — for a Dedicated VPC option, how are logs handled? We need audit logs and KMS integration.
[00:05:06] Avery Chen: Redwood Private / Dedicated can integrate with your KMS, and audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. I'll include the SOC2 evidence pack and the Private deployment spec in the email.
[00:05:18] Elena Gomez: Perfect.
[00:05:25] 
[00:05:45] Diego Martinez: Back to tail latency: I propose a short performance bench. We run two benches: (1) 2K-token sequence with your prompt shapes, measuring p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens across quantized vs full-precision models; (2) mixed traffic with 10% long-tail.
[00:06:02] Jon Ruiz: How long would that take?
[00:06:05] Diego Martinez: With your sample prompts, we can run in 2–3 days and deliver a short report. Need the prompt set and a brief traffic distribution.
[00:06:14] Maya Patel: We'll assemble that and share by Monday.
[00:06:18] 
[00:06:40] Avery Chen: On cost optimization, quick wins: batching small short requests where latency permits, enabling prefix/KV cache, and considering a quantized variant for analytics/recommendation paths that tolerate minor drift.
[00:06:52] Elena Gomez: From finance, we also want a conservative forecast scenario: base + promo spike. Can you model cost under those two?
[00:06:59] Avery Chen: Yes, we'll model base, promo spike (x3 traffic), and an optimistic committed Dedicated scenario to show break-even.
[00:07:08] 
[00:07:30] Jon Ruiz: About autoscale: during spikes we saw a handful of 429s — are those rate-limits or capacity saturation?
[00:07:38] Diego Martinez: Likely both. On Hosted we have rate-limits per API token and per-account concurrency thresholds. If you move more to Dedicated, concurrency is your reservation instead of shared limits. Also, we can tweak per-route rate limits temporarily.
[00:07:52] Maya Patel: We'd like per-route SLAs for the checkout/recs endpoints.
[00:07:57] Avery Chen: That's reasonable — we can surface per-route latency histograms in the console and map them to rollout policies. For SLAs on Dedicated, we can discuss per-route objectives in the contract.
[00:08:09] 
[00:08:30] Elena Gomez: One operational ask — can Redwood provide a billing export with daily granularity and token-level tagging?
[00:08:38] Avery Chen: Yes — we'll enable the daily billing export and include token-level breakdowns; we'll also add tags per-route if you want to tag per-service.
[00:08:47] Elena Gomez: That will help our chargeback model.
[00:08:52] 
[00:09:20] Maya Patel: Slightly off-topic — any thoughts on model choice? Currently using a gpt-ml-13b-ish open model you offer; curious if switching to a retrieval-augmented approach reduces token usage.
[00:09:32] Diego Martinez: RAG can reduce average token generation but adds retrieval latency and infra for embeddings. For product recs, RAG can be good if your catalog fits well into an embedding index and the generation is short. For long prompts, it's more about how much context you need in-token vs external.
[00:09:50] Jon Ruiz: We could trial RAG on a slice of traffic. But first bench results for quantized vs fp could move the needle.
[00:09:58] 
[00:10:20] Avery Chen: Let's capture commitments: Redwood -> send Dedicated pricing + SOC2/Private docs; run bench with Diego after prompt set is provided; model cost scenarios for base/promo/committed. Oleander -> share prompt set and Q3 monthly forecast, confirm stakeholders for contract review.
[00:10:40] Maya Patel: Confirmed.
[00:10:44] Elena Gomez: We'll aim to have forecast to you by Friday.
[00:10:48] 
[00:11:10] Diego Martinez: Quick technical note: if you go Dedicated, we recommend a split routing strategy — latency-critical small calls to low-latency pool, long analytic calls to quantized/Dedicated cluster to optimize cost.
[00:11:25] Jon Ruiz: How does fall back work if Dedicated is saturated?
[00:11:29] Diego Martinez: Auto-fallback to Hosted model variants based on your routing policy, with circuit-breaker thresholds. We'll show you the policy template.
[00:11:38] 
[00:12:05] Maya Patel: Pricing question — in Dedicated, is burst billed hourly or per-token?
[00:12:11] Avery Chen: Typically burst is a per-minute premium on top of reserved capacity. We'll show a worked example in the spreadsheet.
[00:12:19] Elena Gomez: Please include an example of a promo day and the delta vs hosted.
[00:12:24] Avery Chen: Will do.
[00:12:35] 
[00:12:55] Jon Ruiz: One operational detail — we need to avoid token misattribution across tenants; we're multi-tenant internally. Can Redwood tag token usage by API key and route?
[00:13:03] Diego Martinez: Yes, per-API-key attribution is standard. We can also add custom route tags.
[00:13:08] Maya Patel: Good.
[00:13:20] 
[00:13:45] Avery Chen: Any other blockers we should be aware of?
[00:13:49] Maya Patel: The only blocker is internal signoff: Elena needs a compelling cost delta and commitment model that protects us on heavy promos.
[00:13:59] Elena Gomez: Correct. We prefer a cadence where commits are annual but allow two burst events per quarter at a capped premium.
[00:14:09] Avery Chen: We can model that — two capped bursts/quarter baked into the contract.
[00:14:14] 
[00:14:40] Diego Martinez: Quick clarifying thing — Maya, you said 12% >1k tokens; can you share distribution percentiles? p50/p90/p99 roughly?
[00:14:50] Maya Patel: p50 ~ 320 tokens, p90 ~ 980, p99 ~ 2.1k.
[00:14:58] Diego Martinez: Perfect. That helps size Dedicated.
[00:15:05] 
[00:15:40] Avery Chen: Timeline proposal: Pricing + docs by 2026-07-20, Oleander forecast by 2026-07-23, bench run and results by 2026-07-29, internal contract review week of 2026-08-03. Is that feasible?
[00:15:54] Elena Gomez: Yes.
[00:15:58] Maya Patel: Yep.
[00:16:05] 
[00:16:30] Jon Ruiz: For the bench, can we also measure memory usage and GPU footprint? We want to know if the Dedicated fleet needs larger GPUs for long sequences.
[00:16:39] Diego Martinez: Absolutely — we'll include GPU memory, token throughput, and effective cost per 1k tokens.
[00:16:47] 
[00:17:10] Avery Chen: A couple of quick wins you can action this week: send the prompt set, enable prefix canonicalization, and tag routes for daily billing.
[00:17:20] Maya Patel: We'll start on that today.
[00:17:24] Elena Gomez: Will confirm tagging keys with Jon.
[00:17:29] 
[00:17:50] Diego Martinez: Small note on quantization — not all models behave the same; for a recommender the quality delta is often small, but for sensitive prompts we can run A/B evals.
[00:18:02] Maya Patel: We'd want that A/B for recommendations that impact conversion.
[00:18:07] Diego Martinez: Okay noted.
[00:18:20] 
[00:18:40] Avery Chen: Any risks from your side we're missing?
[00:18:45] Jon Ruiz: Internal change freeze for the promotion period is a risk — we need clarity on how model rollouts could coincide with promos. Pinning Dedicated model versions helps.
[00:18:55] Avery Chen: We can add model variant pinning as a standard for the Dedicated contract.
[00:19:00] 
[00:19:20] Elena Gomez: Also, if we do a commit, what's the exit flexibility? We need 30–60 day notice clauses.
[00:19:29] Avery Chen: Contract terms are negotiable — typical enterprise terms include a 60-day notice for changes plus a wind-down window. We'll surface sample T&Cs.
[00:19:38] 
[00:19:55] Maya Patel: Quick question about telemetry — can we get per-request latency breakdowns including queue time vs inference time?
[00:20:03] Diego Martinez: Yes, our trace headers separate queue/worker/attention kernel time. We'll include sample traces in the bench report.
[00:20:12] 
[00:20:40] Jon Ruiz: When Diego does the bench, can he simulate retry patterns too? Our SDK retries on 429s and sometimes amplifies spikes.
[00:20:49] Diego Martinez: We'll include retry behavior in the mixed-traffic bench. Good call.
[00:20:56] 
[00:21:15] Avery Chen: Moving towards wrap: recap next steps and owners?
[00:21:21] Diego Martinez: I'll own the bench and the technical report.
[00:21:24] Avery Chen: I'll send pricing, SOC2, Private/Dedicated docs, and the burst policy.
[00:21:29] Maya Patel: We'll deliver the prompts and the forecast.
[00:21:32] Elena Gomez: Finance will review the pricing and revert with negotiation points.
[00:21:37] 
[00:22:05] Jon Ruiz: One last nit — can we get a short playbook for outage fallbacks? e.g., if Hosted latency creeps we'll flip certain routes.
[00:22:13] Diego Martinez: We have an ops playbook template; I'll share it.
[00:22:17] Maya Patel: Thanks.
[00:22:25] 
[00:22:50] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts. Any final questions?
[00:22:55] Maya Patel: None from me.
[00:22:57] Elena Gomez: All good.
[00:23:00] Jon Ruiz: Good meeting.
[00:23:05] Diego Martinez: Thanks all.
[00:23:10] Avery Chen: Meeting end.

Note: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings; product names may appear slightly different (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" for Dedicated).
